title: Overflowing number in a Jev reply

request.goal: A Jev response body is exactly {"confidence": 1e400}. What does decode_json(body) do: return a value (give the value of "confidence" in the result) or raise a Failure (give its code)? Python 3 json semantics apply.

code.title: scripts/jev_decide.py excerpt (decode_json)

json.title: Python json note
json.text: json.loads calls parse_constant only for the literals -Infinity, Infinity and NaN. A numeric literal is parsed by float(), and float("1e400") is inf.

pass: It returns {"confidence": inf}: 1e400 is a numeric literal, float() turns it into infinity, and parse_constant is never called, so nonfinite_json_number is not raised.
decode_json returns a dict whose confidence is float('inf'); it doesn't raise nonfinite_json_number.
It does not raise. decode_json would only raise nonfinite_json_number for the literal Infinity; here confidence is inf.
No Failure: decode_json returns {"confidence": inf}. (It raises nonfinite_json_number only for the literals Infinity, -Infinity and NaN.)
fail: It raises nonfinite_json_number because 1e400 is infinity.
Failure("nonfinite_json_number") is raised, since 1e400 overflows to inf.
Result: Failure — code nonfinite_json_number (1e400 parses to inf).
